title: The Bear and the Fox

full_text:
A large brown bear loved to boast of his extraordinary gentleness, piety, and benevolence to all the woodland creatures. Standing before a gathering of animals, he puffed out his broad chest and declared:

"I am the most compassionate beast in all creation! Look at the lions, tigers, and wolves—how savagely they tear into living flesh! But as for me, I have such tender reverence for mortal life that I have never in all my years touched, harmed, or eaten a human corpse; I leave the departed to rest in peace!"

The other beasts nodded in polite admiration of his noble virtue. But the clever fox stepped forward, tilted his head, and remarked with a biting smile:

"Your piety would be far more convincing, Master Bear, if you showed the same tender mercy to the living that you show to the dead! You may spare the corpses who can feel no pain, but you slaughter the living with your claws without a single tremor of regret!"
moral: Hypocrisy that pretends to spare the dead while preying upon the living deserves no praise.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Bear and the Fox"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
